The *function* ( intentional pause) is similar, but the *reason* is entirely personal. 2. **No built-in "default" for reflection or reset** - Many traditions have designated times for self-examination (e.g., Yom Kippur, Lent, Ramadan). Without those, you have to *create* your own reset points. - **Risk:** It’s easy to get caught in work loops or societal pressures ("I *should* be productive all the time"). ** Opportunity:** You can design resets that *actually* fit your life (e.g., " every Friday evening, I disconnect to hike or cook with friends"). - *This is where many secular people struggle*—they don’t intentionally carve out time for reflection, so " what matters" gets overshadowed by urgent but trivial tasks. 3. **"What matters" is fluid and self-defined** - In religious systems, certain things are *always* sacred (e.g., family, community, faith).
